rationale: The terminal-bias identity controls the norm excess on every minimizing path; its two interior mean biases are nonnegative.
from_statement_quote: Consider iid edge FPP on Z^d, d>=2, with a<=tau_e<=b almost surely, 0<a<b<infinity. Let h(x)=E T(0,x), g its limiting norm, rho=min_{|u|=1}g(u), and u any minimizer. For integer n>=sqrt(d), round nu to v_n and put L_n=|v_n|, C=(b/a)sqrt(d), K0=bd/2+rho sqrt(d)/2, B_n=h(v_n)-g(v_n), Lambda_n={z in Z^d:||z||_1<=(b/a)||v_n||_1}, and A_n=2|Lambda_n|+1. Let D(0,v_n) be the maximum distance of all minimizing paths to the segment [0,v_n]. Suppose q>=0, alpha>0, K>=1 and E exp(alpha |T(0,w)-h(w)|/|w|^q)<=K for every nonzero lattice w. Then for s>=0, P(D(0,v_n)>sqrt(C L_n (B_n+K0+3s)/(2rho))) <= min(1,A_n K exp(-alpha s/(((C+1)L_n)^q))). If B_n<=H n^q log(2+n), choosing s=(((C+1)L_n)^q/alpha) log(A_n K n^p) gives probability <=n^(-p) and a threshold O(n^((1+q)/2)sqrt(log n)) for any fixed p>0. No independence of the centered passage times is used; this is an upper bound along one rounded direction and does not assert matched global exponents.
to_statement_quote: Let T be an integrable, translation-invariant undirected lattice FPP metric, h(x)=E T(0,x), and g a norm with g(x)=lim_m h(mx)/m on lattice x. Write b(x)=h(x)-g(x) and X(x,y)=T(x,y)-h(y-x). Then b(x)>=0. If z lies on any attained minimizing path from 0 to v, then g(z)+g(v-z)-g(v)=b(v)-b(z)-b(v-z)+X(0,v)-X(0,z)-X(z,v) <= b(v)+X(0,v)-X(0,z)-X(z,v). In particular, if the three centered errors have magnitude at most s, the detour is at most b(v)+3s. No upper bound on the two interior mean biases is required.

rationale: The segment-distance bound includes longitudinal overshoot and turns a geometric detour into a quadratic cost.

rationale: The selected norm direction and bounded rounding defect supply the quadratic norm lower bound without asserting uniform curvature.

to_statement_quote: Let g be a norm on R^d with g(x)<=b||x||_1, b>0. Let rho=min_{|u|=1}g(u)>0 and choose a minimizing unit u. Then g(x)>=rho|x| for all x and g(u)=rho. For integer n>=sqrt(d), round coordinates of nu to obtain v_n in Z^d. If delta=sqrt(d)/2 and K0=bd/2+rho delta, then v_n!=0, |v_n-nu|<=delta, and 0<=g(v_n)-rho|v_n|<=K0. This supplies a lower detour direction and no upper-curvature assertion.

rationale: The deterministic subadditive sequence has centered concentration on every scale but a mean bias n^beta.
from_statement_quote: Fix 0<beta<1. Put h(0)=0, h(n)=n+n^beta for integers n>=1, and T_n=h(n) deterministically. Then h is subadditive, lim_m h(m)/m=1, and E exp(alpha |T_n-E T_n|/n^q)=1 for every n>=1, alpha>0 and q>=0. Nevertheless h(n)-n=n^beta is not O(n^q log n) for q<beta. This is a counterexample to a generic inference, not an iid lattice FPP law.
to_statement_quote: REJECTED INFERENCE: abstract subadditivity of h(n)=E T_n and a centered exponential concentration envelope alone do not imply h(n)-n lim_m h(m)/m=O(n^q log n) on that envelope scale. An FPP subadditive approximation theorem requires its additional stochastic and geometric hypotheses. This concept records a failed shortcut, not a theorem asserting the shortcut.

rationale: The l1 norm has a lower quadratic bound at the selected direction and an unbounded ratio to any upper quadratic bound there.
from_statement_quote: For g(s,t)=|s|+|t| on R^2 and u=(1,0), u minimizes g on the Euclidean unit circle. For |t|<=1, g(u+(0,t))-g(u)=|t|>=t^2. There is no finite C such that g(u+(0,t))-g(u)<=C t^2 for every sufficiently small nonzero t, since the ratio is 1/|t|. This norm example makes no assertion about the limit shape of any particular iid FPP law.
to_statement_quote: REJECTED INFERENCE: a norm satisfying a lower quadratic transverse bound at a supporting outer-sphere direction need not satisfy an upper quadratic transverse bound at that same direction. The direction in a lower-bound argument cannot be reused in an upper-bound argument without verifying the upper hypothesis.
